key_insight: A fully discrete mixed-dimensional model couples porous flow, viscoelastic deformation, and frictional fracture contact, with proven discrete existence, uniqueness, stability, and a priori error estimates.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports numerical analysis of fractured porous materials where fluid flow, deformation, and fracture slip interact.
method: Represent fractures as co-dimension-one interfaces coupled to Darcy flow in the matrix and fractures.
Combine linear matrix viscoelasticity with normal compliance and Coulomb friction at fracture surfaces.
Discretize using conforming finite elements in space and implicit Euler time stepping.
evidence_signal: A numerical experiment computes numerical errors and compares them with the theoretical estimates.
watch_item: The abstract reports one numerical experiment, leaving performance across complex fracture networks and broader loading conditions unestablished.
paper_title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
